In the next four minutes, you'll understand your first real Python program.
A program that prints a medicine label, like this one.
And then, we'll break it on purpose, and see what Python does.
Here's the program. Five lines. Let's run it the way Python does: one line at a time, from top to bottom.
Line one starts with a hash sign. That's a comment: a note for humans. Python simply skips it.
Line two: print. Print means: show this on the screen.
The words inside the quotes are shown exactly as written. Text in quotes is called a string.
Line three prints the drug name. Every print starts on a new line.
Line four has three items, separated by commas. Python shows them one after another, with a space in between.
Line five has a small calculation. The star sign means multiply.
Python first works out 500 times 3, which is 1500, and then prints the answer.
Four instructions, in order, from top to bottom. You've just understood your first program!
Now, let's break it. On purpose.
In this program, line two uses a word Python has never heard of: weight.
Python runs line one. Then it stops at line two, and tells you exactly what went wrong.
Name error: name weight is not defined. And line three never runs.
Just like a pharmacist who stops at an unclear line on a prescription.
Now look at this one. Line two is missing its closing bracket.
This time, nothing is printed. Not even line one.
Because before running anything, Python checks that the whole program is written correctly.
A writing mistake like this is called a syntax error. Syntax means the grammar rules of the language.
Three mistakes almost every beginner makes.
One: writing Print with a capital P. Python is case-sensitive, so always use small letters.
Two: copying code from WhatsApp, with curly quotes. Type the quotes yourself.
Three: forgetting the quotes around text.
Remember, errors aren't failures. They're Python pointing at exactly where to look.
Quick check. What does this line print?
The answer is B: Dose, 500 mg. Python did the multiplication first. Super!
Print shows text and numbers on the screen. A hash sign starts a comment.
Python runs your code one line at a time, from top to bottom.
And errors tell you exactly where Python got stuck.
